Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Start: 09:30 PST
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Aisha, Marco, Li, Samir, Priya, Elena

Summary: Quick sync to align on roadmap milestones and final launch readiness items for the q4 feature rollout (model serving changes, autoscale, canary plan). Also a short incident review reference from last week's regression.

Topics:
- Launch checklist status
- Canary + perf validation
- Autoscaling and Dedicated vs Hosted fallbacks
- Security/SOC2 gaps and audit items
- Incident review notes and follow-ups

Action Items (captured above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha: okay everyone thanks for joining, let's try to keep to 75 minutes, we have a lot to cover for the launch readiness for the model serving changes. I'll kick off with status.
[00:21] Marco: yeah quick heads up from eng ops, we've merged the quantized runtime change into staging but there are a couple of tail-latency anomalies on long sequences. Li is digging into it.
[00:36] Li: mm-hmm, the main issue looks like a KV cache miss spike when sequences cross the 2k token boundary, probably an edge case in the cache eviction. reproduces locally but it's intermittent in staging so i'm running memory + profiler sweeps now.
[00:58] Samir: is that related to the new continuous batching config? we bumped max-batch to 64 in staging to improve throughput, could be interaction there.
[01:15] Li: could be, i saw correlation with higher batch sizes, especially when the prefix cache isn't warmed. so we should test batch=16 as the canary config rather than 64 to keep latency disciplined.
[01:40] Aisha: ok noted — for canary let's target batch=16 and KV cache enabled. Marco, can you own the canary traffic plan?
[01:50] Marco: yeah i'll prepare the traffic split and rollback plan, Samir and i will coordinate. i'll aim to have the config ready by Tuesday 2026-11-23.
[02:05] Priya: from comms perspective we need the NOC contact list and the post-canary incident review slot so we can notify downstream teams. i'll draft the comms template.
[02:20] Elena: also flagging the UX experiment — we need a short user-study script so we can validate if the smaller batch impacts perceived latency for the front-end chat experience.
[02:40] Aisha: good point. Elena, can you run a quick guerrilla test during the canary window?
[02:49] Elena: yes I can do a 2-day run during the canary and share results.

[03:10] Marco: quick question on Dedicated vs Hosted fallback — if canary shows regressions, are we okay to serve from dedicated capacity for critical customers? that has cost implications.
[03:25] Samir: technically yes, we have reserved pools but we'd need to ensure model variant compatibility — quantization profile differences might cause drift. We should have a validated variant matrix so switching doesn't break client expectations.
[03:48] Aisha: i'll add variant compatibility to the checklist. we talked about cost vs latency tradeoffs last week — for launch we want reliability first. we'll revisit cost after week-one telemetry.

[04:05] Li: security note — legal asked for an update on SOC 2 artifacts. We have most controls in place but there are two remaining items: key rotation docs for KMS and a clearer audit log retention policy. I'll draft the SOC2 gap doc and share with legal.
[04:28] Priya: i'll follow up with legal and get a timeline for sign-off. we should make launch contingent on closing any high-severity SOC2 gaps.

[04:50] Aisha: incident review: last Thursday we saw a regression where a background deployment caused 503 spikes for 10 minutes. Samir, can you summarize root cause?
[05:02] Samir: yeah, the rollback didn't clear ephemeral KV caches properly which caused a cache thrash under load; SRE mitigated by draining instances and forcing cache warmup. root cause is the graceful shutdown hook not waiting for the cache to persist. fix is in PR, but we need to add test coverage.
[05:28] Li: adding a graceful drain handshake in the runtime will help. also we'll add a canary check that exercises shutdown flows in staging.
[05:45] Marco: i've got a task to add a post-deploy smoke check that validates no 5xxs for 5 minutes at low traffic.

[06:05] Aisha: ok, let's walk through the launch checklist items quickly — the doc in confluence shows most items green, a few yellow. Marco, which are yellow?
[06:15] Marco: autoscaling policy, canary config, and the runbook for rollback are yellow. we need SRE sign-off for the autoscaler thresholds.
[06:30] Li: for autoscale thresholds i propose: p95 latency target 350ms, scale-up at 70% GPU util, scale-down at 30% sustained for 5m. that keeps tail-latency tight but reduces thrash.
[06:52] Samir: agree on the util thresholds but let's ensure we have a cooldown window so we don't oscillate during sudden traffic spikes. 3 minute cooldown seems okay.
[07:08] Aisha: noted — Marco, please finalize autoscaling doc with these numbers.

[07:22] Priya: on the org side, who signs the launch? do we need VP approval?
[07:29] Aisha: yes product + eng + security sign-off. i'll collate approvals; target to get them by end of next week.

[07:45] Elena: user research quick ask — can we instrument a small latency banner for the test cohort so we can see if users notice the difference?
[07:55] Samir: we can add a lightweight client-side ping metric in the canary. low overhead.

[08:10] Aisha: timeline check: canary planned for week of 2026-11-23, full rollout week of 2026-11-30 if canary is good. Does that still work for everyone?
[08:20] Marco: tentative yes, dependent on Li's perf sweep results.
[08:27] Li: i'll have perf sweep results by 2026-11-25. if we see memory leak or tail-lat issues we will stall.

[08:40] Priya: communications — we should prepare both internal and external messaging. internal first — status updates, then a short external note after launch stable.

[09:00] Aisha: ok quick technical deep-dive: Samir can you summarize the quantization and kernel changes and any compatibility risk?
[09:12] Samir: yes — we used a mixed-precision path and a new attention kernel optimized for longer sequences. For quantized variants we added asymmetric quantization for embeddings. The risk is slight distribution shift on edge prompts; we've run evals on the held-out prompt set and saw <0.5% quality drift but it's worth running more canary evals.
[09:38] Marco: do we have a rollback variant that is bit-for-bit backward compatible?
[09:44] Samir: we have a non-quantized variant that is compatible but cost is higher. we should document the cost delta.

[09:58] Aisha: good. let's ensure the canary includes quality checks (prompt evals) in addition to perf. Elena — can you pick a 50-prompt set?
[10:08] Elena: will do, i'll pull from last quarter's key prompts and include a couple of edge-case prompts.

[10:25] Li: one more SRE note — we need to validate HSM/KMS rotation during canary, don't want key rotation surprises.
[10:34] Priya: legal asked that too. i'll escalate to security.

[10:50] Aisha: any blockers we haven't covered?
[10:55] (brief silence)
[11:05] Marco: i just want to reiterate we need test coverage for graceful shutdown and a smoke test post-deploy. else we risk the same 503 regression.
[11:14] Samir: agreed, PRs are queued. i'll prioritize tests.

[11:30] Aisha: recap and next steps: Marco will finalize autoscaling and canary traffic config; Li will run perf sweeps and share results; Samir will prep rollback variant and tests; Priya will coordinate comms and legal; Elena will prepare prompt eval set; i'll update launch checklist and drive approvals.
[11:55] Priya: i'll put the calendar invite for the post-canary incident review and NOC standby.
[12:05] Aisha: great, thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcript auto-generated; occasional speaker attribution errors likely. References: confluence launch-checklist link, internal perf spreadsheet, SOC2 gap doc (links shared in chat).
